claims.title: Identity-database traffic may expose passwords and refresh tokens if its unverified transport is plaintext
claims.description: `flow:process:authorization-server>store:identity-database>read-and-write-accounts-and-grants` has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If that internal database segment is not protected, an attacker with an on-path position in `boundary:rewards-cloud` can intercept member account data, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consent records between `process:authorization-server` and `store:identity-database`. The disclosed refresh tokens and codes can then be used against `flow:process:mobile-app>process:authorization-server>token-requests` or `flow:entity:partner-app>process:authorization-server>token-requests` to obtain access tokens. This is conditional on the unknown transport setting, not an assertion that the connection is plaintext.

quotes.text: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:process:authorization-server>store:identity-database>read-and-write-accounts-and-grants` has unverified `encryption_in_transit`, while the attacker still needs a position on the internal cloud path. Impact is high because the flow carries credentials and PII, including refresh tokens that can yield further bearer access.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encrypted database transport
mitigations.detail: Configure TLS with authenticated service identities for `flow:process:authorization-server>store:identity-database>read-and-write-accounts-and-grants`, and record the resulting `encryption_in_transit` setting.

mitigations.summary: Reduce credential exposure in database exchanges
mitigations.detail: Use short-lived, rotated authorization artifacts and avoid returning or replicating token material beyond the authorization server's required operations.

claims.title: Points-ledger traffic may disclose member balances if internal transport is unprotected
claims.description: `flow:process:rewards-api>store:points-ledger>read-and-write-points` has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If this connection is unencrypted, an attacker positioned on the `process:rewards-api` to `store:points-ledger` path can intercept balances and points transactions. The attacker can use the collected financial activity and member-related transaction context to target members and infer their rewards activity; this is conditional on the unverified transport control, not a claim that encryption is absent.

quotes.text: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown transport protection for `flow:process:rewards-api>store:points-ledger>read-and-write-points`; an attacker must first obtain an internal on-path position. Impact is high because `store:points-ledger` holds every member's financial balances and transactions, making passive collection corpus-scale.

mitigations.summary: Require authenticated encryption to the ledger
mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:process:rewards-api>store:points-ledger>read-and-write-points` to TLS or mTLS and validate the ledger peer identity.

claims.title: Request-log transport may expose bearer tokens if its protection is not verified
claims.description: `flow:process:rewards-api>store:api-log-store>write-request-log` has `encryption_in_transit: unknown` while it carries complete request headers. If this internal logging hop lacks transport protection, an on-path attacker can intercept bearer access tokens and request-associated PII while `process:rewards-api` writes them to `store:api-log-store`. Possession of a captured one-hour bearer token enables the attacker to call `flow:process:mobile-app>process:rewards-api>call-rewards-api` or `flow:entity:partner-app>process:rewards-api>call-rewards-api` as its holder until expiry.

quotes.text: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.
Access tokens are signed JWTs that live for one hour, and they are plain bearer tokens.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:process:rewards-api>store:api-log-store>write-request-log` has unknown transport protection and requires an internal on-path position. Impact is high because the flow carries bearer credentials whose possession authorizes access to the internet-facing rewards API.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and mutually authenticate log delivery
mitigations.detail: Use TLS or mTLS for `flow:process:rewards-api>store:api-log-store>write-request-log` and record the verified transport configuration.
Change `process:rewards-api` logging so bearer tokens are never included in events; log a token fingerprint or request correlation ID instead.

claims.title: Account-closure traffic may disclose identity data if the console database hop is plaintext
claims.description: `flow:process:support-console>store:identity-database>close-accounts` has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If the support-console connection to `store:identity-database` is unprotected, an attacker on that internal path can intercept account-closure requests and associated identity information. That data reveals account status and can be combined with information exposed by other identity-database paths to target members; the threat is conditional on the unknown transport setting.

quotes.text: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unverified `encryption_in_transit` value for `flow:process:support-console>store:identity-database>close-accounts`; an attacker needs an internal path position. Impact is medium because the flow exposes member account-status activity associated with the identity database's PII.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS with server authentication, preferably mTLS, on `flow:process:support-console>store:identity-database>close-accounts` and verify the configuration in deployment.

claims.title: A copied identity-database volume may reveal credentials if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:identity-database` has `encryption_at_rest: unknown` and contains password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, consents, and member PII. If the unknown resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker who obtains a backup, snapshot, decommissioned volume, or other storage-layer copy can read those records without authenticating through `process:authorization-server`. Refresh tokens and codes recovered from the copy can then be exchanged through the authorization-server token-request flows. This is conditional on encryption at rest being absent or ineffective for operational copies.

quotes.text: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on `store:identity-database` having no effective encryption at rest; obtaining an operational copy requires storage-layer access rather than an application request. Impact is high because the store contains credentials and PII, and recovered refresh tokens can create additional bearer access.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the identity database and all operational copies
mitigations.detail: Establish and record the at-rest posture for `store:identity-database`; use managed envelope encryption with restricted key use for the primary store, backups, snapshots, and replicas.

mitigations.summary: Limit the value of recovered token records
mitigations.detail: Encrypt or hash token material appropriately, rotate signing and refresh-token secrets, and minimize retained authorization artifacts.

claims.title: A copied points-ledger volume may disclose every member's rewards history if unencrypted
claims.description: `store:points-ledger` has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If its media, backups, snapshots, or replicas are not effectively encrypted, an attacker holding a storage copy can read every member's balance and points-transaction history without using `process:rewards-api`. The aggregate financial activity can be correlated to profile information obtained elsewhere and used for targeted fraud or privacy abuse. This claim is conditional on the unknown at-rest protection.

quotes.text: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:points-ledger` has unknown `encryption_at_rest` and the attacker must acquire a storage copy. Impact is high because the ledger holds every member's financial balance and complete transaction history.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the ledger and its copies at rest
mitigations.detail: Verify `store:points-ledger` encryption at rest and require managed-key encryption for its primary media, backups, exports, snapshots, and replicas.

claims.title: A copied API-log store may yield bearer tokens and PII if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:api-log-store` has `encryption_at_rest: unknown` and persists complete rewards-API request headers, including bearer access tokens. If the store or an operational copy is unencrypted, an attacker holding that copy can recover logged tokens and PII without calling the API. Recovered bearer tokens can be replayed to `process:rewards-api` through its mobile or partner-app flows until their one-hour expiry, making one log-store disclosure an immediate access path as well as a privacy loss.

quotes.text: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.
Access tokens are signed JWTs that live for one hour, and they are plain bearer tokens.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown `encryption_at_rest` setting for `store:api-log-store`; the attacker must obtain a storage-layer copy. Impact is high because the store contains credentials and PII, and a recovered bearer token can be presented directly to the internet-facing rewards API.

mitigations.detail: Redact Authorization headers at `process:rewards-api` before `flow:process:rewards-api>store:api-log-store>write-request-log` is emitted.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and tightly restrict log-store copies
mitigations.detail: Verify encryption at rest for `store:api-log-store`, cover backups and snapshots, and restrict export and key-use permissions as strictly as the source API data.

claims.title: Code executing in the authorization server can read the identity database through its existing grant
claims.description: `process:authorization-server` reads and writes `store:identity-database` via `flow:process:authorization-server>store:identity-database>read-and-write-accounts-and-grants`. An attacker who gains code execution in the authorization server or controls its host can use that component's already-authorized database connection to read member accounts, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents. Encryption at rest would not stop this attacker because the database serves data to the authorized process. Recovered tokens can then be used to obtain access tokens through the authorization-server token flows.

quotes.text: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because the attacker must first gain code execution or host control in `process:authorization-server`, and the model does not state such a foothold. Impact is high because its established database path reaches credentials and PII for the authorization system's member population.

mitigations.summary: Constrain the authorization server's database read scope
mitigations.detail: Use narrowly scoped database roles and separate access paths so `process:authorization-server` can read only the rows and fields needed per operation.
Log database queries under a distinct authorization-server principal and alert on bulk extraction, token-table enumeration, or atypical export patterns.

claims.title: Code executing in the rewards API can read all ledger records through the API's access
claims.description: `process:rewards-api` reads and writes `store:points-ledger` through `flow:process:rewards-api>store:points-ledger>read-and-write-points`. An attacker who gains code execution in the rewards API or controls its host can invoke that established read path to extract balances and points transactions for the whole ledger. The disclosure is independent of at-rest encryption because the attacker acts through the authorized application reader; the collected history can be correlated with other member data and used for targeted abuse.

quotes.text: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because exploiting this requires code execution or host control in `process:rewards-api`, which the model does not establish. Impact is high because the component's stated read path reaches every member's balance and transaction history in `store:points-ledger`.

mitigations.detail: Restrict the database or ledger principal used by `process:rewards-api` to required fields, row scopes, and operations rather than broad corpus reads.
Audit ledger reads by the rewards API principal and enforce rate, pagination, and export limits that detect access inconsistent with member requests.

claims.title: Prefix-matched redirect URIs can send authorization codes to an attacker-controlled endpoint
claims.description: `process:authorization-server` accepts a redirect URI when it merely starts with the URI registered for a partner app. An outside attacker can craft an authorization request using a prefix-matching attacker-controlled redirect endpoint and induce a member to complete sign-in and consent; the authorization server then returns the member's authorization code over `flow:entity:member>entity:partner-app>return-with-authorization-code` to the attacker-controlled destination. The attacker can exchange the captured code through `flow:entity:partner-app>process:authorization-server>token-requests` and obtain an access token, which can then reach the rewards API. HTTPS on the browser return does not prevent this disclosure because the authorization server sends the code to the attacker-selected endpoint.

quotes.text: the authorization server accepts any redirect URI that starts with it.
The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high because `process:authorization-server` is internet-facing and the source states that redirect matching accepts any URI starting with the registered value, making a crafted redirect practical once a member is induced to authorize. Impact is high because the returned authorization code can be exchanged for a bearer access token that reaches the rewards API and its financial and PII-bearing operations.

mitigations.detail: Register complete redirect URIs and require an exact, normalized match at `process:authorization-server`; do not accept prefix, wildcard, or partial matches.

mitigations.summary: Bind authorization responses to the initiating client session
mitigations.detail: Require and validate state and PKCE for authorization-code requests, especially for public and browser-mediated clients, so a captured code cannot be completed by another party.
